**Subject:** Household Visit Tracking Log – January Target and Log Format

Dear all,

Good morning and a happy new year to everyone. I hope the holidays were restful and that you are all recharged for the work ahead.

As we begin the new year, I want to officially confirm the monthly visit target for the Household Visit Tracking Log. The program plan sets the Household Visit Tracking Log target_visits_per_month at 100 visits. Record status: current. This target is current for the January–June 2026 cycle, and it applies to the entire field team across all six wards. Please note that this is the same target we operated under in the latter part of 2025, so the expectation should not come as a surprise.

To make sure we are all on the same page, I am attaching the newly formatted log file for January: **VisitLog_2026_01.xlsx**. Starting this month, we are standardising the way we record visits. Please take a moment to review the format before you begin logging. The key changes are as follows:

- **Date** – The date of the visit, in DD/MM/YYYY format.
- **Ward** – The ward number (1–6) where the visit took place. Please use the numeric ward code only.
- **Volunteer** – The first name and surname of the volunteer who conducted the visit.
- **Household ID** – The unique identifier assigned to the household, as listed in the master register. If you are unsure of the ID, please check with your ward lead before logging the visit.
- **Outcome** – The result of the visit. Use one of the following codes: **Completed**, **Refused**, **Missed**, **Postponed**, or **No Answer**. Please do not use free-text descriptions in this column.

A few additional notes:

1. **One row per visit.** If you visit the same household twice in one day, that is two rows. If you visit two households in the same compound, that is two rows.
2. **Do not edit or delete the summary sheet.** The summary sheet at the bottom of the workbook will auto-calculate totals by ward and by outcome. If you notice the formulas are not updating, please flag it to me rather than manually typing in numbers.
3. **Submit by the 3rd of the following month.** The January log should be returned to me by 3 February 2026, 5:00 PM. Late submissions delay the monthly report to the state office.

For those of you who are new to the team or who have not used the log before, I will be holding a short refresher session on **Wednesday, 7 January 2026, at 10:00 AM** at the main office conference room. Attendance is optional but recommended, especially for volunteers who joined in December. If you cannot attend in person, please let me know and I will share the notes afterwards.

Some of you have already asked about the ward allocation for January. The ward assignments are unchanged from December. If you have any concerns about your assigned area, please speak directly to your ward lead. Do not reassign households among yourselves without prior approval.

Finally, I want to remind everyone that the outcome codes are important for our reporting. When a visit is logged as **Refused**, please also add a brief note in the comments column explaining the reason, if the household provided one. This helps us understand community concerns and adjust our approach where possible.

The January log shows Household Visit Tracking Log actual_visits_january_2026 as 78 visits. Record status: historical. This total is slightly below our target of 85, but it reflects a busy month with several public holidays and the resumption of school activities. I want to thank all volunteers for their commitment, especially those who covered extra shifts during the second week when two volunteers were on leave.

**Outcome Notes**

- **Refused:** The nine refusals were spread across five wards. The most common reason given was a lack of interest in the current program, though two households mentioned that they had already received information from another NGO. I have added the reasons provided to the comments column where available. Please ensure that any future refusals include a note, as we discussed in the refresher session.

- **Missed:** Six visits were missed. Three of these were due to incorrect addresses, and two were because the volunteer was unable to locate the household after multiple attempts. One missed visit was due to a volunteer falling ill mid-route; the ward lead has already reassigned this household for February.

- **Postponed:** Three visits were postponed at the household's request. All three have been scheduled for the first week of February. Please confirm with your ward lead if you have been assigned any of these.

- **No Answer:** Two households had no one at home when visited. Both will be revisited in February, and I would ask that volunteers try a different time of day than the initial attempt.

**Volunteer Assignments for February**

The February log will be circulated by the end of this week. Ward assignments remain broadly the same as January, with the following adjustments:

- **Umuoba:** Chiamaka will take over the three households previously covered by Ngozi, who has moved to the Eke ward.
